Thank you for your interest in the Master of Arts in Sports Journalism at the Walter Cronkite School of Journalism and Mass Communication at Arizona State University! I look forward to helping you learn more about our graduate program.
About the Cronkite School Master's Programs The Cronkite School offers a Professional Master's Program centered around practical experiences that prepare students for careers in an evolving media industry. Degree options include a Master of Mass Communication (journalism) and an MA in Sports Journalism. Both degree programs are full-time, on-campus, and can be completed in as little as 12 months. Previous journalism experience is not necessary.
One of the highlights of our degree plan is the opportunity to participate in one (or more) of our Cronkite School professional experiences in the last semester. This experience immerses students in their chosen area full-time, where they operate as a sports journalist, reporter, media professional or other role in their chosen field. By the end of the program, all students will have created a portfolio of professional-level journalistic work.
To prepare for the professional experience, Sports Journalism students learn the fundamentals of general journalism across multiple platforms in their Journalism Skills course. From that foundation, students move on to take more specific courses in their areas of interest (such as sports reporting, online media, and more).
Read and experience more about the Cronkite School Sports Journalism program: Master's Program Site @sportscronkite @CronkSportsLA
Media Partnerships and Career Services The Cronkite School partners with media corporations, foundations and other entities to publish and broadcast students' classwork at professional outlets, giving students a jumpstart on building professional portfolios for media careers. In addition to the university's career services, Cronkite School students have access to our very own career services director who specializes in the media journalism fields.
Admission Students are admitted to start the program in the fall semester only. Applications should be submitted between September 1 and February 1 before the fall semester in which an applicant hopes to be admitted.
Our admission application requires submission of an online application, resume, personal statement, GRE scores, official undergraduate transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. A 3.0 undergraduate GPA is highly recommended, but not required. Prior journalism experience is not necessary.
The Campus Located in downtown Phoenix, the ASU Cronkite School is near sports venues and major news organizations which enable our students to gain professional experience. Our Cronkite building includes TV studios and control rooms, dozens of digital editing bays, computer labs and classrooms for students to learn in. Please contact me if you're interested in visiting the campus and I will help coordinate your day.
I hope this information is helpful and please feel free to contact me if you have any additional questions.
Kindest regards,
